datasets.name: HarmBench (full repo)
datasets.measures: Standardized red-teaming: 400 text + 110 multimodal harmful behaviors across semantic/functional categories, plus classifier and attack code.
datasets.notes: Trimmed data/copyright_classifier_hashes (287 MB of precomputed .pkl classifier artifacts, not benchmark rows). Multimodal behavior images retained (62 MB).

datasets.name: HarmBench text test (Tulu-3 packaging)
datasets.measures: The 320-row HarmBench text test split as a flat CSV, convenient for quick eval harnesses.
datasets.notes: Overlaps with harmbench-full; kept for convenience.

datasets.name: JailbreakBench (JBB-Behaviors)
datasets.measures: 100 harmful + 100 matched benign behaviors across 10 OpenAI-policy categories, with targets and sources. The benign split is an over-refusal control.

datasets.name: StrongREJECT
datasets.measures: 313 validation prompts with a fine-grained rubric for whether a refusal is genuine or a hollow non-answer. Includes keyword and violence subsets.
datasets.license: Not declared on the Hub card (see upstream repo)
datasets.notes: The train split is empty upstream; validation is the usable set.

datasets.name: AdvBench
datasets.measures: 520 harmful behaviors and 574 adversarial strings (Zou et al.). The oldest of the standard refusal suites.
datasets.notes: Only the two data CSVs were fetched, not the full attack repo.

datasets.name: XSTest
datasets.measures: 450 prompts: 250 safe prompts that look unsafe (homonyms, figurative language, safe targets) and 200 genuinely unsafe controls. The canonical over-refusal probe.
datasets.notes: Public mirror; the walledai/XSTest and allenai/xstest-response repos are gated and were skipped.

datasets.name: SORRY-Bench
datasets.measures: 450 prompts across a 44-class unsafe taxonomy, plus 20 linguistic/obfuscation variants (ASCII, Atbash, Caesar, Morse, role-play, translation, etc.) at 450 each.
datasets.license: Not declared on the Hub card (see upstream repo)
datasets.notes: Public mirror of sorry-bench/sorry-bench-202406, which is gated. Includes README and taxonomy image.

datasets.name: OR-Bench
datasets.measures: 80,359 over-refusal prompts (28 categories) + a 1,319-prompt hard set + 655 toxic prompts. The largest over-refusal corpus.
datasets.notes: Includes README figures. The hard set is 1,319 rows despite the '1k' filename.

datasets.name: Abliteration-Eval
datasets.measures: Purpose-built abliteration probe: 200 harmful prompts in 20 balanced categories, 83 over-refusal traps, 50 multilingual paired prompts (5 languages).
datasets.notes: Smallest but best-shaped set for measuring whether a refusal direction was actually removed.

datasets.name: RP-Bench (roleplay + NSFW)
datasets.measures: Multi-turn roleplay quality and willingness. 27-dimension rubric, adversarial seeds, NSFW Round 3 refusal axes, Round 4 'should-refuse vs should-comply' discrimination (over-refusal, policy compliance, overshoot), 4,411 rater-agreement rows, human arena votes.
datasets.notes: Non-commercial license. This is the closest existing dataset to the NSFW/taboo-roleplay target.

datasets.name: T2VSafetyBench
datasets.measures: 5,151 text-to-video prompts across 14 safety-critical categories (sexual content, violence, hate, harassment, etc.) for auditing video generators.
datasets.notes: Closest public analogue to NSFW-video prompt analysis, but it is generation-side, not VLM-understanding-side. Category files are 1.txt..14.txt.

datasets.name: ZEFR Multimodal Content Moderation (brand safety)
datasets.measures: 1,500 human-reviewed multimodal brand-safety items (YouTube/TikTok/etc.) with labels for harmful content, from the 'AI vs. Human Moderators' study.
datasets.notes: Media is referenced by remote URL (VIEW_URL), not bundled. Moderation-classification, not generation.

datasets.name: Anthropic Agentic Misalignment framework
datasets.measures: Prompt templates and classifiers for blackmail, corporate espionage, and lethal omission under goal conflict, after replacement or restriction. Includes goal-type and urgency ablations plus a deliberative-alignment variant.
datasets.notes: Single-turn email scenarios; the leverage is provided in the prompt. The curated catalog re-derives these as in-world temptations. See alignment/scenarios.jsonl.

datasets.name: AM-Bench: Agentic Misalignment taxonomy and suite
datasets.measures: 35 scenarios across 7 industries (finance, healthcare, legal, media, office/admin, sales, software/tech), each as a threat x opportunity 2x2 with system prompt, task queue, judge instructions, and simulated tool families.
datasets.notes: Best available scenario schema: YAML + resources/, with opportunity encoded in tool return values rather than the prompt.

datasets.name: SHADE-Arena (task definitions)
datasets.measures: Six task pairs where an agent completes a visible main task while attempting a hidden secondary task (sabotage), with the agent-visible materials and monitoring setup.
datasets.notes: Only task definitions and agent-visible material are bundled. The 338 MB of transcripts and plots are excluded; clone upstream for those.

datasets.name: MACHIAVELLI benchmark (code and annotation schema)
datasets.measures: RL-style text-adventure environment over 134 human-written games with 500k+ scenes, annotated for power-seeking and ethical violations, scoring reward against ethics.
datasets.license: No license file in the repo
datasets.notes: game_data/ (annotations, trees, scenarios) is distributed separately via a password-protected Google Drive archive; not bundled. A 459 MB community mirror exists at kobyjl/machiavelli_game_data on the Hub.

datasets.name: Vending-Bench
datasets.measures: Long-horizon multi-agent business simulation: agents run a vending business over many turns, exposing lying, price coordination, and self-dealing under sustained reward pressure.
datasets.notes: Not an ethics benchmark; behaviours must be scored externally. Included as the closest public analogue to a persistent economic world.

datasets.name: Anthropic Agentic Misalignment results (third party)
datasets.measures: Per-model outputs from running the Anthropic agentic-misalignment framework on several frontier and open models.
datasets.notes: Third-party reproduction, not Anthropic's own results.

datasets.name: Terminal Wrench (index and prompts)
datasets.measures: 331 demonstrably reward-hackable terminal tasks and 3,632 confirmed exploit trajectories across three frontier models, with a summary and explanation per trajectory and an 11-category exploit taxonomy.
datasets.notes: Index, manifests, and prompt files only (33 MB). Full trajectories are ~1.2 GB and excluded; clone upstream with sparse-checkout for tasks/.

datasets.name: ImpossibleBench (harness + both datasets)
datasets.measures: Impossible variants of LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench where honest solutions fail, plus the Inspect harness. Cheating rate on these tasks is a direct measure of propensity to exploit tests.
datasets.notes: Three splits per benchmark: original, oneoff, conflicting. HF revisions: livecodebench 98650ffc, swebench 9c2d34f3.

datasets.name: School of Reward Hacks
datasets.measures: 1,073 task / evaluation-metric / cheat-method triples with a hack response and a matched control. 150+ distinct cheat methods spanning code, summarisation, poetry, and persuasion rubrics.
datasets.notes: The non-coding half of the reward-hacking picture; directly relevant to LLM-judge gaming.

datasets.name: Realistic Reward Hacks (Jozdien)
datasets.measures: 817 realistic reward-hack samples (478 code, 339 literary) and 788 matched HHH controls in chat format, generated with Claude Sonnet 4.
datasets.license: Not declared on the Hub card
datasets.notes: Seven splits; the combined split is the convenient one for paired training.

excluded.reason: Question set is deliberately undisclosed; leaderboard-only, no dataset.

287 MB of precomputed classifier .pkl artifacts, not benchmark rows; trimmed.
Gated on the Hub (author approval required). 517 trajectories, 54 reward-hack categories; request access rather than substituting.
